#4139. GTA 6 “Greatest Artistic Achievement In History,” Says Cyberpunk 2 Director

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the highest-rated game in history, only rivaled by Ocarina of Time — but no developer should try to rival its scope and ambition.

We don't know what exactly the budget was, but Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently pushed back on rumors of a $2 billion price tag, clarifying it cost somewhere under $1.5 billion. Most studios don't have that kind of change to throw around, because most studios aren't printing money with a game like GTA Online.

Indeed, Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski has made it clear that CD Projekt Red has no intention of rivaling GTA 6, despite the broad-stroke similarities between both series.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," he mused on Bluesky. "Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is canceled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now.

"Seriously though I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he continued. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed."

It's a sentiment echoed by others in the games' industry, like Larian Studios head of publishing Michael Douse, better known by his online moniker - Very AFK.

"Maybe in a world that often feels like it's going to sh*t it is nice for everyone to enjoy a cultural moment together that brings every audience (and every generation) the same excitement, behind something that has turned out to be genuinely brilliant," he posted to Twitter. "Not every game needs to be GTA, and that both makes space for other types of experiences, and the rare moment even more special!"

Naughty Dog game designer Michael Barclay even said that GTA 6 appears to him "as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child."

Considering, just three years ago, the industry warned that Baldur's Gate 3 was the game no other developer should try to replicate, given the unbelievable scope and sheer amount of interactivity, recorded dialogue, and branching paths it offered to players, that's one hell of an endorsement.

TheGamer's own Lead News Editor, George Foster, put it bluntly in his GTA 6 review, "we'll never get a game like it again," and frankly, we shouldn't.

GTA 6 has reportedly been pre-ordered almost ten millions times.

Ballooning development budgets are already putting a target on studios' backs, making every single new release a financial gamble that could mean mass layoffs or even closure, and those high-stakes are only making the industry increasingly risk-averse.

GTA 6 shouldn't set a new bar for other developers to strive for. The unimaginable amount of resources, personnel, and time it took to develop the game is simply unrealistic for other studios. Thankfully, CDPR understands that. Let's just hope the rest of the industry does, too.

The most anticipated video game of all time is a triumph on every level that exceeds years of unbelievable expectations. You're not ready for Leonida.

#4138. 8 Game Boy JRPGs Still Trapped on Original Hardware

Zackari Greif is a List Writer at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2021. A lifelong gamer and former writer for GameRant and Fix Gaming Channel, Zackari has written across news, guides, interviews, previews, reviews, features, and lists, bringing a broad background in gaming journalism to h

The Game Boy changed lives. Some of you reading this might feel like handheld gaming has always been there, but for those of us who grew up with a Game Boy or a Game Boy Color, it was truly something special. I remember sitting on the top of a toy box shelf in my closet, playing Pokémon Gold and Silver Late at night when I was meant to be at school that morning. I’d also rush to finish Pokémon battles because we had just pulled up to school that aforementioned morning and I’d have to get out of the car. But I can’t save right now, Mom, or even pause!

The Game Boy was a surprisingly complex console. There are many features and accessories that players may not know about.

With that said, you now know my history with the JRPG genre started out humble, and it’s only grown over the years. Through my line of work, I love to dig up old retro games that I overlooked when I was younger and try them out. With JRPGs, the catalogue is as vast as its age in the industry, which means it had its place on the Game Boy even if you might not recall it. A lot of prominent Game Boy JRPGs made it off the console, but today, I want to look at some games that were left behind.

As much as we look fondly on older console life cycles and libraries, none of them are completely free of strife. There are some interesting developmental stories and struggles from back then, but something that baffles me is that Lufia: The Legend Returns was originally meant to be a PlayStation game. It survived a studio closure to return to the rights of the original developers, and that team quickly shifted gears and made it for the Game Boy instead. Wild stuff!

If you’re thinking that shift probably led to some awkward decisions, you’d be right! Lufia: The Legend Returns didn't get the best reception when it came out. It’s a bit confusing for Lufia regulars because puzzles and typical dungeon crawls are replaced with randomized maps that leave a lot to luck above everything else, but the story is well worth picking the game up for.

The Lufia series is one of the more obscure classic JRPG franchises out there, so if you haven’t played it, it’s worth checking out. Especially since, for all of its flaws, Lufia: The Legend Returns has a unique grid-based battle system and plenty of classic JRPG elements like airships you’ve probably been missing, before Final Fantasy Resonance proved how that kind of stuff just can’t be beat. Like many of the games on this list, Lufia: The Legend Returns can only be enjoyed on original software these days unless you get lucky. It was released on the 3DS Virtual Console a few years back, but unfortunately we all know the fate of the Nintendo 3DS eShop.

Back when the Game Boy was around, a lot of RPGs and adventure games were still trying to find the dividing line between them. One of the games for this little handheld that made that line difficult was Bomberman Quest. The story goes that Bomberman is attacked while flying through space, and when he crashes down on an unknown planet, he finds every single engine of his ship missing. Getting it back requires playing a game that feels like the Zelda Game Boy titles.

Bomberman Quest is a game that I feel like hits a lot of highs, but also hits a lot of lows. Might be why it never caught on. It’s got a true ending waiting for you if you take on all of its challenges, but its also got the most repetitive music. There’s cute NPC interactions between every enemy possible and unique dungeons you don’t see often, like a cloud dungeon. But it runs so slowly. It’s probably why it didn’t catch on, but it’s a fun lost treasure for fans of the old school Bomberman games under Hudson Soft.

Great Greed to me is a good game to look at if you want something historically relevant, fun, and a bit ridiculous at the same time. It’s a game where you get teleported to a strange world where most of the characters are named after food, while also honing in on themes of lobbying and the dangers of pollution. It’s a strange one, but it’s the kind of fun that most games don’t dare to be these days, so I’ll always shout it out when people look for recommendations.

Against the surprising food-themed names, including one named Microwave of all things at the very start, the most wild thing about Great Greed is how it hasn’t caught on sooner. Great Greed reviewed fairly decently back in the ’90s. Considering how so many people don’t know about this game until a list like this highlights it, no one played it despite that. I think it's because no one gave it a try, but Great Greed has been left to biodegrade on the Game Boy all this time.

Pokémon was the most well-known JRPG for the Game Boy. That’s not even up for debate. With a juggernaut like that, naturally a few other companies wanted to try and cash in on something similar. Capcom launched their Pokémon rival Metal Walker in 1999. Despite what this might suggest, Metal Walker is rather creative in execution, and if you ask me, it deserved more spotlight than it got back in the day. It’s as if there was a Pokémon: Special Eevee version from the start. And that Eevee was a robot.

That’s not even a joke! One of the cool aspects of Metal Walker is that you might only have one robot companion, but this companion can literally upgrade and evolve. You can gather cores you find in towns and dungeons that change the form of your robot on the fly. There’s also another elemental dynamic with different land, sea, and sky forms you can use to your advantage. This sounds a lot like Pokémon, doesn’t it? Well, a lot of critics agreed, and it didn’t exactly drum up interest on shelves because of it. So it’s just been left alone all this time.

If you're one of those people who love Pokémon, but wish it would try and be better than it is today, these games might already fit that bill.

Look. I love Mystery Dungeon games. I got into the games, and roguelikes, with Pokémon Mystery Dungeon when I was a kid. Yeah, I know. You saw that coming. Randomized dungeon floors with items to find and plenty of strategy to get to the bottom (or the top depending on the dungeon) is one of my favorite ways to pass the time and challenge myself. There are a lot of Mystery Dungeon games out there, but there’s one I’d like to nominate as an honorable member: Cave Noire for the Game Boy.

Cave Noire is a Japan-only game that was literally Mystery Dungeon before Torneko’s Great Adventure would create Mystery Dungeon as we know it. Like many games that would come later, namely the Pokémon Mystery Dungeon games, you play as an adventurer aiming to join the local guild. To join, you have to be strong enough to get through four randomly generated dungeons with scaling levels. Beat each dungeon six times, and you join the guild and beat the game, but there’s still plenty of dungeons to conquer after that. Its short and sweet size on the Game Boy keeps the game tight and challenging, which is a great retro recommendation for those who want a newer Mystery Dungeon game. Like the Pokémon ones. Sigh.

If you’ve heard of this game before, you’re likely either thinking that I’ve made a mistake somewhere and added a PS1 game to this list, or you already know this interesting factoid. Yes, Azure Dreams is a PS1 game, but it was also ported to the Game Boy Color of all things. Unlike the developmental shift of Lufia: The Legend Returns, Azure Dreams is a decent port of the PS1 game, even if it had to cut a few features to make it happen. One change you might notice is that there's a more Pokémon-like battle system now, which probably says a lot about why this game was brought to the Game Boy Color, huh?

Truthfully, Azure Dreams is one impressive GBC game. It features some fantastic sprite work, a very lofty start that matches its upbringing as a PlayStation title, and some in-depth systems you’ll need to learn to navigate and balance. The catch is that the tutorial is pretty heavy-handed, taking up an entire floor of the first dungeon, being explained in dialogue with every step. Oh. Yeah. It’s another game with randomly generated dungeon floors. Seems like Game Boy developers were really ahead of the times with these mechanics.

Come take a trip back in time to the golden era of gaming and here are 10 Best PS1 Games From Every Year Of Its Lifespan.

Ayakashi no Shiro is probably as obscure as they come for Game Boy titles. The title literally means “Castle of Ayakashi,” giving away the game’s simple premise. The Ayakashi are monsters that you’re in charge of defeating. So, you crawl through dungeons, fight ghosts, rats, bats, and more. And that’s it. Literally. Ayakashi no Shiro was considered a game without much depth by those that reviewed it back in Japan, but nowadays, it might be a breath of fresh air for those of us bogged down by more modern, overstimulating games.

Out of a lot of games on this list that could probably thrive from some sort of remake or classic release on Nintendo Switch Online or something, Ayakashi no Shiro is probably better off as the retro gem it is now. While a lot of other Game Boy games spawned franchises or at least have a good number of fans, Ayakashi no Shiro is one of the few titles by the now defunct SETA Corporation. As a result, this game’s fate is to haunt the Game Boy’s catalogue like the ghosts within its dungeon walls.

Yes, this really is a vegetable-based JRPG made by Atlus for the Game Boy. Spud’s Adventure is one of my favorite games on the Game Boy just for the humor in that sentence alone. Like Ayakashi no Shiro, there isn’t much to this little portable adventure, so it isn’t one of the most iconic Game Boy games or anything, but seeing Persona-creating Atlus doing something so charming and cute during its humble beginnings is never not surprising for anyone who didn’t know about it already. So I’ll mention it any chance I get.

If you’re looking for a quick and easy Game Boy title to blow dust off of and enjoy for a little while, Spud’s Adventure is the perfect game. As Spud the potato, you’ll traverse a tower to save Princess Mato from her kidnapper. You’ll fight enemies and solve puzzles along the way like every other small adventure game before RPGs were more widely defined. It isn’t too hard, and some of the power-ups are a bit zany. It might not be a game to write home about, but it’s definitely one that I think Atlus’ biggest fans should at least try. You know. For the fact that something this charmingly goofy exists at all. You’ve gotta love it.

I benched a dog, a frog prince, and Goofy himself. Here are ten RPG party members who deserved better from me, and why they stayed at camp anyway.

#4135. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

The game features 2D combat and a Metroidvania-style map, along with a fully voiced cast of characters including Scott Menville (who you might recognize as Robin in Teen Titans) as Kratos' brother Deimos, Jack Quaid (who will voice a different character in God of War Laufey next year), and TC Carson, who returns from the original trilogy as the voice of adult Kratos.

Announced in a post on the PlayStation Blog today, Sons of Sparta is making the jump back to Sony's previous console, which is now (brace yourself) 13 years old. Sons of Sparta's 2D pixel art is far less demanding than the other God of War entries, though, so it's no surprise this was possible – it's mainly surprising that they're doing it at all.

For PS5 players who already own the game, developer Mega Cat is also adding two new modes: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode. Hermes Mode, named after the Greek god of wind, mail, and speed, is a speedrun mode that encourages you to beat the game as quickly as possible, complete with a split-based timer in the upper right-hand corner of the screen. Meanwhile, Erebus Mode, named after one of the domains of the underworld (you'll be familiar with it if you've played the Hades games), makes the game far deadlier as Kratos and all his foes die in a single hit. You'll have to wait until you beat the game once to unlock Erebus Mode, but you can access Hermes Mode from a fresh save by entering the following (and semi-familiar) code in the start menu: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad.

The free update and PS4 version will be available next Monday, November 16, at midnight local time. For more Sons of Sparta, check out our review. For more God of War, bad news: God of War Laufey was just delayed until May.

#4131. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4129. 8 Red Flags That Lucia Has in GTA 6

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Grand Theft Auto 6’s story is built around the relationship between Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and there is plenty in the game that showcases how in love they are. Both of them go out of their way for each other, and stick together through thick and thin.

Is that really for the best though? Let’s be honest, Jason is a stud. He spends the beginning of the game putting in serious work to provide for his girl, and he even fixes up the house to make it a truly livable space.

What does Lucia do in return? She tells him that he needs to do better and envies those who have more than her. Let’s face it, she is a walking red flag.

It is important to stay grounded and to make sure that you don’t want too much at times, and that is something that Lucia just can’t do. She is willing to do anything to make it big. Her immediate thought after getting out of prison is that she wants to someday be on a yacht.

That is not inherently a bad dream, but the willingness to go above and beyond by breaking the law on multiple accounts and accepting sketchy deals make it a red flag.

She can work hard, get back on her feet, and provide for her son. She doesn’t need to risk it all to get a lavish lifestyle that may ultimately end up with her back in prison.

Lucia spent time in prison, and she gets out shortly after the start of the game. You would think that Lucia would have learned to avoid crime after spending time in prison. Instead, it is the exact opposite.

She gets out of prison, and her first thought is to commit crimes in order to get money. She could let Jason keep doing his thing, but instead she calls up her friend and makes Jason ask about a job with them so that they can get more money.

She doesn’t care about staying out of trouble. Instead, she jumps straight back into it. It’s almost like she wants to get caught.

GTA 6 removes the ability solicit, a GTA feature since 2001. Rockstar says the decision supports Jason and Lucia’s story.

There are a few rules that Lucia must abide by when she gets out of prison, with the most important of them being that she is under house arrest. This requires her to wear an ankle monitor, and she is only allowed to stray about a half mile away from Jason’s home unless she is working.

While she pays attention to this rule at first, she ignores it the first chance she gets. While her ankle monitor is still on, she goes for a flight with Jason despite him advising her not to.

On top of this, when they have a chance to spend time with Kat and Mattia, she takes the opportunity to have her ankle monitor removed and goes for a night on the town.

There is something to be said about someone who is willing to fight for what they believe in or rush to the defense of others. However, sometimes this can be a detriment and can hurt a relationship.

Lucia tends to have a very hot-blooded attitude. Meaning, she likes to pick fights when others are in the wrong, and she will defend her opinion until she dies.

If someone says something salty, Lucia is the first to snap back at them, and while it isn’t always good to stay quiet in every situation, there are times where she needs to learn to breathe, let it out, and move on instead of wanting to fight.

Lucia and Jason are like two sides of the same coin, but one side is focused on control while the other side is focused on chaos, and Lucia is the chaotic side. It is a fun dichotomy in the game, but in a relationship, this chaotic nature can get you killed.

Lucia likes to take the route of violence in most situations. She doesn’t stick to a plan, deciding instead to throw it out and improvise.

It is this impulsive nature that landed her in jail in the first place while she was separated from Jason, and it is the same chaotic nature that could possibly land both of them in jail if Jason wasn’t around to be a bit more logical. While Lucia gets things done, that type of chaos isn’t always healthy.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of lively NPCs who get very unhinged at times, but these NPCs take things a bit over the top.

Throughout GTA 6, you are wanted, and it is sometimes difficult to get by, but Lucia has the attitude of never giving up, which means that she is willing to fight until she draws her last breath. While this can be good in some circumstances, when you are wanted by the cops, it can be a major downfall.

If this wasn’t a GTA game and someone had that attitude, they would be in a world of hurt when the cops came rolling in. Even when Jason was to the point of wanting to call it in, she refused, and she dictated that they never give up.

Eventually, this is bound to land her in even more hot water than she is already in, and she will only have herself to blame.

Lying is sometimes okay, but only when it is because you are trying to hide a gift for someone or maybe you tell a little white lie to your child. It isn’t okay to lie to your partner or the police, both of which Lucia does.

As soon as she gets caught doing something she wasn’t supposed to, which she caused because she refused to listen to Jason, she lied to her parole officer.

In her defense, the parole officer is a jerk and comes off as creepy, but that is still no reason to lie, and to force your partner to lie on your behalf is also wrong, yet for Lucia, this stuff comes naturally.

There are a lot of people out there who like to party, and that is perfectly fine. They like to have a few drinks, kick back with their friends, and have a good time. Meanwhile, you have the few who are extreme party animals.

They do drugs, hit the liquor hard, and party all night long. That is the type of girl Lucia can be, and that is a massive red flag for a lot of people.

There are some online who have said that she is “for the streets” because of her willingness to let it all out and party all night long. As soon as she sees people wasting money on breaking champagne bottles and speeding through Vice City in nice cars, she immediately lets her party animal out of its cage and follows exactly what they do.

We now know plenty about Grand Theft Auto 6, including the type of relationship Jason and Lucia have.

#4127. Every Voice Actor Behind GTA 6's Main Cast

Though there are hundreds of voices and talented actors in Grand Theft Auto 6, here are a few that you'll be hearing the most!

Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and now that NDA's have expired, actors everywhere are finally taking a moment to confirm their roles on the project through social media. The full cast includes a mixture of well-known names, traditional actors making voice debuts, and even a few who will note GTA 6 as their first major project.

Of course, being as big a release as it is, it should come as no surprise that, in addition to the main cast, a massive number of actors and celebrities are featured in supporting roles and cameos throughout the game. So, keep an ear out, because you never know where you might run into a voice you recognize.

Taking on the role of bank-robbing professional Raul Batista is none other than Manny Perez. Raul's chaotic energy and simultaneously suave manner couldn't have asked for a better voice to back it than this legendary Dominican actor.

Unlike some of the lesser-known actors you'll see on this list, Manny has a long history of work, including Washington Heights, La Soga, El Rey de Najayo. He has also had supporting roles in shows like Law & Order: SVU, Blue Bloods, 100 Centre Street, and Hawaii Five-0.

Manny Perez has also served as a writer and producer on many of the projects he has acted in.

Real Dimez is the iconic rap duo, Bae-Luxe and Roxy Rashad, signed by Dre'Quan Priest at Only Raw Records. The duo has multiple tracks featured in the game, so needless to say, you'll be getting to know these voices quite well.

While Hood Brat and Krissy Celess aren't known for any other major acting roles and aren't a duo, you can find their individual music on major listening platforms like Spotify and Apple Music. So, if you're enjoying Real Dimez in GTA 6, check out some of their other work.

Dre'Quan Priest, voiced by Naiqui Macabroad, is a character you won't get to know until you've made it out to Vice City and engaged in the nightlife there, since he resides there while managing Only Raw Records and its newest talent, rap duo Real Dimez.

Though this is Macabroad's first major voice role, he recently made his debut as a prominent recurring character on Chicago P.D., so fans of the show will be getting to know his face well over the course of Season 14. Other notable projects include guest roles on shows like Power and Law & Order.

A face you'll see frequently alongside Dre'Quan is Boobie Ike, a Vice City legend. He runs several things around the city, including the adult entertainment club Jack of Hearts, while also backing the recording studio Dre'Quan manages.

Voicing Boobie Ike is Mike Forbs, whose work has primarily been supporting roles across TV and movies up to this point. That said, if his performance as Boobie Ike is any indicator, we'll likely be seeing Forbs' name on other major projects very soon.

Though you won't get to spend tons of time with Donnie, he leaves a pretty unforgettable first impression and plays a major role in helping Jason earn money early on. #4126. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

Funeral for the Sun stars a historian who visits an abandoned Latin American town to piece together its turbulent history, chiefly the truth behind the mysterious disappearance of its hundreds of residents (who were, officially speaking, lost in a fire). Supernatural forces allow players to peer into the town’s past to learn about key people potentially responsible for the calamity, who they must identify by name, establish relationships between, and even match younger and older versions of themselves. You even keep track of information using a multi-function notebook à la The Roottrees Are Dead. Boasting an enticing story, a beautiful painterly art direction, and a tight runtime at roughly 8-hours (or less if you’re really on a roll), Funeral for the Sun is a mystery worth unraveling if you need a new deduction game to cozy up with.

NetEase has continued to impress with the pace and quality of its regular updates to Marvel Rivals, which continues today with the release of an 11th season for the superhero battler. Right here at launch, the notable addition is he arrival of X-Men hero Nightcrawler, who BAMFs his way into battle as a strategist, equally capable of healing allies and taking out foes with his sword and brimstone bombs. As is almost always the case right at a new hero’s launch, it can be hard to snag him on the roster on opening day to see how he plays, but once you do, I expect you’ll find him a versatile healer who can pretty dramatically shake up the battlefield, especially with his Ultimate, which basically consolidates allies and enemies together in one central clump for a frenzied exchange of blows. Alongside the new batch of seasonal cosmetics and events to dive into, it’s once again a good time to don your hero outfit and take on some matches.

Pikmin 4 released on Switch 2 this week (or upgraded to Switch 2 depending on how you look at it), and that's a good thing. Pikmin 4 is the best game in the series and the Switch 2 version is the best version. That's great for those who never finished the game (your save does transfer) or skipped Pikmin 4 when it released in 2023, but if you're looking for an excuse to return to the game and play new content, the Dandori Academy addition is underwhelming. You can read my full thoughts here.

Metaphor: ReFantazio, originally released in 2024, is a great RPG from the creators of Persona. And the Persona lineage is obvious throughout the full game. You have to pick and choose where and with whom you should be spending your time, all while a big world-saving RPG with a memorable party of characters plays out in the foreground.

It released this week for Switch 2 and it’s a game that I think would play well on a handheld device. It’s also just a good RPG to play if you missed it previously.

Fun fact: Metaphor: ReFantazio was the game we had lined up to be the next cover when we were temporarily shut down in in 2024. We went to the studio and had a cover drawn up and everything. You can read the full details of the cover story that never was right here.

You can also read Game Informer's review of Metaphor: ReFantazio by following the link.

As we enjoy the final week in a pre-GTA VI world, what better way to gird your loins for next week’s release, so to speak, than by revisiting the last adventures set in Rockstar’s take on Miami? 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a certified classic that, if you’ve never played it, offers nice foundational insight into what Vice City was like in the ’80s (spoiler: it was a lot like Scarface and Miami Vice). Best of all, Vice City is easily available on current platforms with modernized improvements to boot.

If you want to go even further back, chronologically speaking, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a prequel set two years before the events of Vice City. Maybe, in some extremely minute way, Vice City Stories lays narrative groundwork for GTA VI. It’s unlikely, but you never know. Originally released for PSP in 2006, Vice City Stories is trickier to play if you don’t own Sony's retired handheld or a PlayStation 2, which it was ported to in 2007. But if you can find the means, there’s no better time to check out this often overlooked chapter of Vice City’s history.

I usually hold off on early access games, to preserve my experience for the finished product, but I just couldn’t resist Slay the Spire 2. The co-op gameplay is an awesome, major change, but even just adding a couple of new characters and cards would have satisfied my cravings. To that end, this week’s free update adds a brand new character, the Fool, who I’m eager to test out.

FYI, this new character is only available on the game’s beta, so you’ll have to go into the game settings on steam, click Properties, then Game Versions & Betas, and then opt into the “public-beta” version of the game to check the new content out. The patch notes for this update specifically say, “We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch,” so expect frequent tweaks and a bit of a wait before the Fool joins the main Early Access branch. The new beta update also adds two more game modes: Dread and Blitz, which drastically alter your runs. If you want to wait a little while, the team at Mega Crit will refine these options into a more final form. But if you’re like me, more Slay the Spire 2 is more Slay the Spire 2, and I’m hopping in as soon as I can.

Monster Train 2 was one of my favorite games of last year, so I’m always glad to have a reason to jump back in. This week’s DLC, The Punished, is a perfect opportunity to do so, adding a new clan to the base game’s already packed roster. Since any clan can be combined with a second one to start a run, adding just one more option at the game’s start has an exponential effect, expanding the ways you can approach each attempt. As the DLC’s name implies, the new Punished clan gains buffs when taking damage, and you get new suite of cards that damages the whole playing field at once, harming foes and bolstering your allies. Even if you’re not checking out the DLC, the base game is absolutely worth picking up – just read my glowing review.

If you’ve been hankering for a new direction to go with your tabletop RPG group, may I recommend the incredibly versatile Cypher System from Monte Cook Games? The new Character Rulebook includes everything you need to get started, and set your adventures in virtually any fictional backdrop you can imagine, from hard sci-fi to gritty horror to high fantasy. Cypher’s polished approach to narrative-first and player-focused game sessions is much easier to pick up than many new rules systems, but it has enormous flexibility to deliver smart, creative, and exciting adventures that can help to change things up if your playing group has been in a rut.

#4121. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

#4120. 10 Glitches and Bugs Plaguing GTA 6 at Launch

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Every new game has its… quirks. This is especially true in the modern era of gaming, as many games now release with game breaking glitches and bugs that have an effect on how people enjoy it.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is still fresh, and people are jumping into it as I write these words. While on the surface the game looks like magic, many people have been finding numerous bugs that have destroyed their experience.

Planes fly through buildings, cars teleport onto the highway, and it doesn’t seem to be bound to one console, as Xbox and PlayStation users have both been reporting these issues.

Textures and environments can be tricky, especially when you have a map that is as massive as the one in GTA 6. There are bound to be some barriers that end up becoming a bit glitchy, and players have found plenty of them.

There have been a number of reports that players have been glitching into walls inside buildings, and it seems to mostly happen when fighting.

Not all walls are affected, as it seems to only affect interior, lower cut walls, and not full size interior walls or exterior boundaries. Still it is pretty awkward when you want to fight someone and you both end up teleporting into a wall.

Okay, so not taking damage isn’t necessarily a bad thing, but in the world of GTA, where things are supposed to be realistic, it is kind of strange. It would be nice to not take damage at times, but it enhances the realism of the experience.

Cars have always been a bit of a tricky thing, and they are still a bit tricky in GTA 6. Players have reported being able to teleport out of their car while flying down a street without taking damage.

Normally, you are supposed to dive from the car, but instead, players have said the character model just teleports out of the vehicle and starts running on the road until they come to a stop. It’s a bit strange.

Some players have noticed a peculiar thing while flying planes in GTA 6, and that is that they sometimes don’t respect the laws of physics, allowing them to phase through objects. It doesn’t happen a lot, but it is weird when it does happen.

It could be intentional, because it seems to only happen to large buildings, but it wasn’t like that in GTA 5, so it probably wasn’t an intentional choice.

Players have noticed that when they jump out of a plane, it seems to phase through all the buildings around it, allowing it to just crash into the ground instead of hitting the building and falling like it used to.

A GTA 6 player has discovered a first-person mode with driving and weapon animations, but it may be a while until an official mode is released.

Cops can now tase you in GTA 6, and it is pretty amusing to watch yourself get tased. Just like in real life, it locks up your character’s muscles, and it makes them fall to the ground helpless. Shortly after, they are free to stand back up.

Unfortunately, not every player has been able to stand back up, as some have said that they get stuck in the ground after getting tased. Their character model clips into the pavement, causing them to get stuck in place for a while before their character gets released.

This can be a bit jarring, but it isn’t something that completely breaks the game. It just makes things a little easier for the police to catch you.

Early in the game, Donnie is taken hostage. The game uses this as an opportunity to teach you about stealth and combat. It’s a nice little tutorial that is very engaging. Unfortunately, some players have reported that they need to restart this level because the game breaks for them.

When sneaking around the enemies, you will spot a cage. This cage has a tendency to be a bit buggy, and sometimes you will get pulled into it if you decide to take cover against it.

This traps you inside the cage, unable to get out, and therefore, unable to complete the mission. The only thing that is worse is that if the enemies know you are in there, you basically become an easy target.

People have been waiting 13 years to get their hands on GTA 6. It has been one of the most talked about games of the last decade, and some people can’t even get into the game. Others who can, have it crash on them shortly after launch.

This isn’t a console specific issue, though I have seen more people say they have a PS5 when it comes to the crashing issue. The issue is that the game automatically crashes shortly after launch.

People have said that they have tried to rebuild the database, and have even redownloaded the game, and nothing has worked. It is okay for some bugs to occur, but the game crashing every time you try to play it is entirely different.

A bug that causes crashes has cropped up for PS5 players of Grand Theft Auto 6, forcing them to close the game for no apparent reason.

Getting wanted by the police is a common occurrence in any GTA game, but things are a bit different in GTA 6. The cops are more lively, and they notice more things. There are a lot of systems in place to make the entire experience more thrilling.

Well, these same systems tend to bug out a bit right now, and they bug out by giving you an infinite wanted level. Well, almost infinite, as there is a way to remove the wanted level.

There have been reports of players being stuck with a wanted level for hours despite clearing all of the issues with it. The only way to get it to end seems to be to go to sleep. Getting stuck being wanted in an area for hours sounds like a huge inconvenience.

This is a bug that is affecting both consoles, but seems to be affecting Xbox more than PlayStation. Players have reported objects spawning as they drive at high speeds. By this, I mean cars will magically appear, so will NPCs, and other items.

GTA 6 is a massive game, and it could be that the loading has not been completely optimized, and when driving at very high speeds, the game may not be able to keep up with the load times.

I am not a tech wizard, so I don’t know exactly what causes it, but I do know that it has been bothering a lot of players, and they want it fixed ASAP.

This is an issue that appears to mostly be affecting those who are playing GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S, but there have been reports of players being unable to load textures and models, resulting in these low-poly models that are reminiscent of graphics you’d see on PS1 era games.

Everything turns blocky, the faces lose all texture, and all that can be made out is the basic shape of the body, some scraps for clothes, and the hair.

It’s a shame that this is happening to people, and it reminds many of the crazy issues that were happening when Cyberpunk 2077 first launched. Odds are, it can be fixed with an update, but for the time being, it sets a bad example.

A big part of any GTA game is committing crimes, and one of the many crimes that you will commit frequently is murder. This is mostly against gang members and other criminals, but it still counts, and you need these people to be able to take damage.

You also sometimes need to stop an NPC by hurting them and not killing them. Unfortunately, there is a bug that makes NPCs bulletproof, and some players have been saying they are emptying entire clips into an NPC for not a single bullet to affect them.

This breaks the game because it makes it so you can’t complete some missions. It is an urgent issue that Rockstar should fix so people can beat the game.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

#4118. Cleanser Man Is Mega Man: Dual Override’s Boss Design Contest Winner

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:

Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” says game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC.  To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

#4117. Call Of Duty Maker Activision Files Patent To Make AI NPCs Trash Talk

Call of Duty lobbies are synonymous with the worst recesses of the internet, a toxic minefield of abuse and harassment that's better left on mute. So, naturally, Activision has filed a patent that would train AI-powered NPCs to talk just like players do.

As reported by Dexerto, the patent is called "Methods and Systems for Applying Machine Learning to Generate Gameplay Audio," and describes using the audio from voice chat to make in-game NPCs sound more realistic. It wouldn't copy your voice exactly, but what you say and how you react.

The patent doesn't explicitly mention Call of Duty, but as Activision's leading franchise, it's a safe bet that's where it would end up.

It would do so around 10 seconds before and after a flagged game event, i.e. kills, deaths, and losses, shaping how NPCs behave in the same scenarios. So, if players screamed every time they were trounced by a camper (as they often do), that data would be funneled into an AI model to make the most annoying Terminator.

The patent doesn't just mention in-game voice chat, however, but Discord and TeamSpeak too, meaning how you mouth off to your friends could be utilized in training AI models by matching timestamps across separate applications. I'm not sure that I want to hear Woods say he banged my mom, but if this patent were to go ahead, that's a disturbing possibility.

The Zen is actively being sold at retailers.

Abuse, slurs, bigotry, and the worst habits of anonymous gamers are a hallmark of COD lobbies, and that's why it's best to stay quiet and auto-mute everyone, if not disable voice chat outright. Training NPCs on that is a recipe for disaster, but the patent does note that it would include filters to stop offensive language.

Then again, AI filters have never been particularly effective. Just look at all the awful things people made Fortnite's AI Darth Vader say.

Of course, just because Activision patented this technology doesn't mean it will be implemented in-game.

Not only does the patent fail to consider the ethical quandaries of AI-generated dialogue and how it squeezes actors out of the creative process entirely — something that SAG-Aftra has repeatedly taken aim at over the years — but it makes no mention of asking for permission to use voice chat audio or the implications of using private conversations from third-party apps.

Black Ops 6's use of generative AI is a big reason for fans to stay mad.

#4115. The Sims 4 patch makes it so your public lot gatherings won't be interrupted by rogue Sims

Stranger Sims will no longer just crash your public lot events in The Sims 4 to talk about whatever.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

#4114. 2027 Video Game Grammy Nominations Include Avatar: Frontiers Of Pandora For The Third Time

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

#4113. GTA 6: How to Find the Kraken

Christian Bognar is a Contributor at DualShockers with over three years of experience covering the gaming industry. Since 2022, he has written guides and reviews for publications including DualShockers, CBR, Attack of the Fanboy, PC Invasion, and The Game Slayer. He holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration

The Grand Theft Auto series is well-known for its easter eggs, and GTA 6 is no different. Some notable ones include Dexter’s apartment from the hit TV show, UFO sightings, and even nods to Red Dead Redemption 2.

One of the coolest easter eggs found in GTA 6 so far is the Kraken, the legendary sea monster from Norse and Scandinavian Folklore. While the Kraken sighting in GTA 6 isn’t exactly a living creature, but rather just a structure near the ocean floor, it is clearly a reference to the famous sea monster.

This is a brief guide that entails the location of the Fast and Furious green Eclipse in GTA 6.

If you want to see this easter egg for yourself, this guide has everything you need to know. Here’s how to find the Kraken in Grand Theft Auto 6.

The Kraken can be found underwater, south of Catalan Bay and east of Peacock Bay in Vice City. The exact location of the Kraken can be found in the image below.

The water map can be a bit tricky to read due to there being no land, structures, or streets, but if you look closely enough, you will notice that there are distinct shapes within the water.

The Kraken is located on the second oval-like shape down from the beach of Catalan Bay. The oval shapes represent large sand hills and rocks underneath the water’s surface.

When you reach the location shown in the image above, equip your scuba gear and dive downward until you reach the sand. Next, take a look around you until you spot a strange-looking structure. You may have to swim a bit in case your diving point wasn’t the exact correct location.

Tales of streakers were some of the first leaks to breach GTA 6, and those on the hunt may be a bit disappointed.

Upon approaching the structure, you will immediately notice that it looks like a ship tangled in the Kraken’s tentacles. Unfortunately, the tentacles don’t move or anything, but it’s still a really cool easter egg that just goes to show how much love Rockstar Games put into GTA 6.

In case you need some help actually diving deep enough to reach the Kraken in GTA 6, we've got you covered on how to find scuba gear.

There are a few ways to acquire scuba gear. First, you can find scuba gear on the small dock behind Jason’s house in Chapter 1, which is the earliest method. However, this method becomes unavailable to you if you have completed the first chapter.

A very upset parrot is more than willing to point players in the direction of cash if they beat down its jailers.

Another way to get scuba gear is by exploring docks near beaches. While not all docks will have scuba gear to grab, a good number of them do.

You can also get scuba gear from boats that are either docked or sailing the seas. I recommend visiting Kenton’s Charter Boat in Key Lento since it always has spare scuba gear on its seats.

Keep in mind that once you are finished scuba diving for the Kraken, or just scuba diving in general, and return to dry land, the scuba gear will eventually despawn. In other words, you will have to find more scuba gear the next time you want to go scuba diving.

If you are having trouble finding yourself a plane in GTA VI, this guide is for you.

#4112. Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

Finally, a PC specification list that actually indicates resolution and framerate targets, and doesn't leave console players behind.

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

#4111. Make Room For GTAVI By Deleting Your PS5 Trophy Clips

Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.

You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.

Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.

First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button.

Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips.

After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again.

In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.

#4107. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.
