#4106. 10 Best Games That Showcase The Xbox Brand

Eric Warner is a Journalist and Multimedia Producer based in New England with over 7 years of experience producing stories for multiple publications

Microsoft’s gaming brand, Xbox, has finally reached the momentous milestone of existing for 25 years, with all four generations of Xbox console greeting gaming memories that will last lifetimes for those who played them throughout the 21st century.

These days, however, in the wake of poor direction during the Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S eras, Xbox is struggling to retain a healthy gamer population, with many gamers choosing instead to play games on Nintendo or PlayStation due those platforms’ vast variety of exclusive titles.

With Xbox having recently reached its 25th anniversary and the next generation of Xbox consoles, Project Helix, expected to debut in a few years, here’s a look back at 10 exclusive games that best showcase the Xbox brand and may potentially entice people to try an Xbox console.

Many fans of the British game developer, Rare, likely recognize them for creating Nintendo-centric titles like Banjo-Kazooie or Donkey Kong Country but under Microsoft’s ownership, one of the best games they ever released was Viva Piñata.

A life simulation game, Viva Piñata is set on the wondrous Piñata Island and has players restore a garden there with the goal of attracting, raising, and defending the local population of living piñata animals so that they can be eventually shipped off across the globe to become the center of attention at parties.

Viva Piñata encapsulates how creative, fun, and unique Xbox games can be and, while there hasn’t been a new Viva Piñata game in over 18 years, people today can still easily play it and other classic Rare games via the compilation Rare Replay.

One of the best games that showcases the absolute power and capabilities of modern Xbox consoles is Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, the latest entry in the long-running Microsoft Flight Simulator series.

Like many flight simulator games, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 allows players to learn how to fly planes in both first and third-person but this game is the most advanced flight simulator yet as players can learn how to fly other real and fictional aircraft in numerous locations across the globe.

For example, people can fly Halo’s Pelican dropship over Yosemite National Park, the Goodyear Blimp over London, a DG Flugzeugbau DG-1000 over Mount Fuji, a Airbus Helicopters H225 over the Stilt Villages of Papua New Guinea and more.

From Minecraft Legends to Gears of War: E-Day, these 10 great games defined the Xbox Series X|S and showcased Xbox's ever-changing modern identity.

Viva Piñata was very memorable but it wasn’t the most popular video game Rare made under Microsoft’s ownership, with that title instead going to the hit cartoonish pirate multiplayer game Sea of Thieves.

Played primarily in first-person, Sea of Thieves allows players to create and customize their very own pirate and ship as they set sail alone or with a crew of friends into monster-infested waters in search of treasure and glory across the sea.

Sea of Thieves might have had rough start when it first launched in 2018 but in the years since, it has truly shined to become the definitive pirate multiplayer experience thanks to its comedic gameplay and eventful updates adding new areas to explore and supernatural sea creatures to fight.

For a while, Xbox was the best platform to play western RPGs on and, during the original Xbox era, one of the best exclusive games to showcase this status was Bioware’s legendary Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic.

A third-person round-based RPG, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic is set roughly 4,000 years before the events of the Star Wars films and follows an amnesiac warrior as they set out to stop the Jedi turned Sith Darth Malak from conquering the galaxy with the mysterious Star Forge.

While KOTOR’s gameplay hasn’t aged perfectly in the 23 years since its launch, its story, characters, and world designs have remained immaculate, with its characters going on to influence many other Star Wars stories and it still featuring one of the greatest gaming twists surrounding the character of Darth Revan.

Since the days of the Xbox 360, Microsoft has often invested and supported small game developers with immense potential, leading to the release of games like Braid, Ori and the Blind Forest, and the subject for this entry, Cuphead.

Studio MDHR’s debut title, Cuphead is a 2D run and gun game with visuals inspired by rubberhose-style cartoons of the 1920s and 30s, similar to Steamboat Willie, following the brothers Cuphead and Mugman as they set out to collect soul contracts from various bosses in order to save their souls from the Devil.

While Cuphead was only a timed exclusive on the Xbox One, it represents the brand’s ability to support small game development studios and uplift experimental titles into gaming stardom as Cuphead has gone on to sell millions of copies and become a highly successful multimedia franchise.

From PUBG: Battlegrounds to Cuphead, these 10 great games defined the Xbox One and helped entertain players through Xbox's darkest era.

Racing has always been at the core of Xbox gaming from the early days of Project Gotham Racing to the more modern Forza Motorsport titles and while none of these games have been as popular as Mario Kart, one has managed to become the most advanced, realistic racing game yet: Forza Horizon 6.

The latest entry in the ongoing Forza Horizon series, Forza Horizon 6 has players take to the urban and rural streets of Tokyo, Japan in over 500 cars as they strive to qualify for the Horizon Festival or simply explore the many beautiful landscapes of Japan alone or with friends.

In a similar way to how Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 became the premier modern flight simulator, Forza Horizon 6 has become the premier realistic racing game thanks to its hyperrealistic visuals, vast automotive and track customization options, and dynamic environments.

KOTOR is one of the best RPGs to ever debut on an Xbox console but it’s not the brand’s premier exclusive RPG, with that honor instead going to 2004’s Fable and the greater Fable franchise.

Originally pitched to be a fantasy RPG that would have allowed players to have kids in-game, and witness plant life grow among other promises, the original Fable wound up being a very charming, British humor fantasy RPG following a young boy as he set out to become the hero of Albion.

While the first Fable didn’t meet all of its creator, Peter Molyneux, aspirations, it sequels did slowly start to achieve all of Molyneux’s promises and more, becoming the source of many fond memories to the point that Forza Horizon 6’s own Playground Games is rebooting the series with 2027’s Fable.

One of the most recent games that best showcase the Xbox brand’s storytelling capability and multiplayer potential is The Coalition’s Gears of War: E-Day, the sixth mainline entry in the Gears of War series and prequel to the first Gears game.

Like its predecessors, Gears of War: E-Day is a third-person cover shooter with updated maneuverability but what made it really shine is its emotional story following COG soldiers Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, Mags Carter, and Lucas Reyes as they face the first horrifying Locust invasion on Emergence Day.

Gears has always been known for its gory, action-packed gameplay as well as its heartfelt story following people face seemingly insurmountable nightmarish forces and E-Day proves that Gears can still deliver horrifying, emotional yet hopeful gaming narratives 20 years after its first debuted in 2006.

From Kinect Star Wars to Halo 3, these 10 great games defined the Xbox 360 and the era when Xbox was at the top of the gaming industry.

The Xbox 360 era was arguably Xbox at its best and most successful largely in part due to Microsoft investing in several permanent and timed exclusive titles alike, such when Microsoft and Mojang worked together to make the Xbox 360 the first console home for the global sensation that was Minecraft.

While Minecraft was already highly popular on PC, Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition helped introduce millions of console players to the blocky survival game for the first time via Xbox Live Arcade in 2012 and led many to grow up with the game as it evolved and expanded with every update.

Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition’s success ultimately led to Microsoft acquiring Mojang in 2014 and since then, the two companies have worked together to make Minecraft one of the most successful multimedia franchises of all time through the release of numerous Minecraft updates, spinoffs, and adaptations.

The Halo franchise is as integral to Xbox as Sonic the Hedgehog is to Sega and Super Mario is to Nintendo and while there have been many fantastic Halo titles released over the years, I would argue that the best entry in the series to showcase the Xbox brand is the FPS prequel, Halo: Reach.

Bungie’s last Halo title, Halo: Reach has players embody the customizable Spartan-III Noble Six as they join the Spartan-II and III squad of Noble Team in defending the human military world of Reach from an alien Covenant invasion a few months before the events of Halo: Combat Evolved.

While Reach’s campaign is a ton of fun on its own, I believe Reach is the best Halo title to represent the Xbox brand because it remains the most complete Halo title to date as it launched with four-player campaign co-op, playable Elites, Firefight, Forge, Theater, Infection, Grifball, and more fun modes and features.

From Project Gotham Racing to Halo: Combat Evolved, these 10 great games defined the original Xbox and set the groundwork for Xbox's future.

#4105. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Just Got A Free 1.2 Update, Adding New Game Plus

The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the year's biggest, most ambitious games, and the developers over at Rebel Wolves have done a good job cleaning up bugs and performance issues in the weeks since launch. Today, that trend continued; the new 1.2 update is out now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and it adds New Game Plus.

The new mode is uniquely ideal for a game like Dawnwalker. The narrative is very player-driven, whether it has to do with your literal dialogue options, your ability to manage your vampiric hunger, or the order you complete quests, and all of these elements can cause your experience to vary wildly. It makes sense, then, that players would want to jump back in to try things again and see what might happen if the game is played differently, and New Game Plus allows them to do that while keeping combat fresh.

According to the update notes on the Dawnwalker website, "NG+ unlocks after you complete the game’s Epilogue and lets you experience the story again while keeping your progress – mainly your character level, skills, and inventory." You don't gain access to these skills until you complete the prologue, however, which marks the adventure's proper start.

The new mode will also rebalance the world's level scaling. In the base game, certain areas are much harder than others, but in New Game Plus, all enemies will rise in power to match your level, meaning you can explore the world in whatever order you want. On that note, the level cap has also been raised to 100, and protagonist Coen can collect new, more powerful versions of weapons marked with an "NG+" label.

That's basically everything in this update. Rebel Wolves also added some slight tweaks to combat in the base game and adjusted some geometry in the open world, but the main focus here was New Game Plus. This is in contrast to the 1.1 update, which added a much wider suite of bug fixes and made the game run more smoothly.

#4103. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4100. 8 Hard to Beat Game Boy JRPGs

Shane is a Contributor for DualShockers writing guides and other materials. He has a degree in Game Design and Criticism.

Back in the day we didn’t have a ton of ways to check how to beat something or find any guides that would be readily available. A lot of the time you just sort of muddle through until you figure out exactly what you’re supposed to do.

The Best Game Boy Advance JRPGs That You Need to Play in Fall 2026 are perfect for enjoying while surrounded by the colors of autumn.

Even for some of the best JRPGs available you could spend a ton of hours just getting through one part. It was a glorious time where conquering that challenge felt rewarding because of how difficult that particular JRPG section may have been.

A lot of the games on this list are from series and part of that is because most games that released on the original Game Boy were not JRPGs as they weren’t quite as big in the states. Regardless, any game on this list is sure to give you a rough go of it if you aren’t prepared.

While Rolan’s Curse II is a bit more of an action-RPG, the game still takes several notes from JRPGs at the time and typically is counted amongst them. Instead of traditional turn-based mechanics, the game uses real-time combat making it more difficult than other JRPGs.

Many would go on to call it a Zelda-like game, but thanks to the inclusion of a party system with several characters it does fit the JRPG genre. The real-time aspect of the game made it more difficult to play, but also could force players into continuous encounters making things escalate in difficulty rather quickly.

The original Rolan’s Curse is a bit different from the second entry since it doesn’t include a cast of characters to play as. Much as you might imagine the game centered around the same core principals although the upgrades and such are for your character.

Two things specifically make this one a bit tougher, one being that there’s limited ways to recover yourself and second the combat is fairly punishing. It’s a game that definitely requires you to play with focus and without that focus you’ll find yourself dying a lot.

The very first game to ever be released in the SaGa series, The Final Fantasy Legend has some interesting history behind it. The game featured fantasy and sci-fi elements alongside each other as players built a party to take on the challenge ahead of them.

The difficulty of the game stemmed from how unusual the character development systems were combined with some harder combat as the game progressed. Players who didn’t take advantage of the systems for leveling would find themselves at an extreme disadvantage.

Despite the title of this one, it’s actually the first game in what would eventually become the Mana series. A much closer game to Zelda than many would imagine, but mostly thanks to weapons and such doubling as exploration tools.

Outside of that the game featured a party system in which an NPC could tag along on an adventure to help out. The real difficulty of this one comes from keeping tabs on your timing and positioning where even a small mistake could be costly.

From classic Final Fantasy to Undertale, these 10 JRPGs reward understanding your enemy more than stacking up levels

A strange game for the time period that used a first-person view instead of top down for a fantasy JRPG. It took notes from things like Dragon Quest in terms of giving players the ability to investigate and engage with the world on a deeper level.

Since everything was fairly cryptic and there wasn’t much information given, players could often find themselves stuck on certain parts of the game. It took a lot more effort to get from one place to another if you didn’t want to do the investigating you had to.

This game changed some of the formula from the first one and introduced a tried and true JRPG mechanic, a party system. Rather than controlling one character the player now had a party to manage, but still used a first-person turn-based mechanic for gameplay.

Arguably a bit harder than the first game since now you dolled out resources amongst a party over just an individual. You could, of course, still miss plenty of things without investigating which led to players being at an extreme disadvantage some of the time.

Probably one of the crazier games in the series with a lot of going on in just about every part of the game. The odd fantasy and sci-fi bits of the game mixed gave players a lot of choice in how they handled leveling their character and gaining equipment.

In true JRPG fashion, what makes the game unique also makes it incredibly difficult. By transforming your party members into various races based on items you gave them could really screw up your journey if you weren’t careful.

Many JRPGs of the time period were doing some experimental work with various mechanics to spice up how their games played. Final Fantasy Legend II was no exception to this rule and even took it a step farther making it arguably one of the hardest JRPGs for the time.

Even the best JRPGs have some form of resource management, but those usually don’t apply to the story. MAGI, a collectible resource in the game, could be used to both enhance your character or progress the story forcing a difficult choice between power and story.

Fans of handhelds that like to challenge themselves should definitely check out this batch of Game Boy Advance JRPG adventures!

#4099. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

#4098. Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off A Third Of Its Staff

Firaxis, the studio behind the Civilization series, has laid off around 60 employees, representing a third of its staff. The report comes from Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier.

In a statement provided to Bloomberg by a spokesperson from 2K, a subsidiary of Firaxis' owner, Take-Two, “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

In addition to the 60 affected staffers, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is also departing. Bloomberg also reports, via anonymous Firaxis employees speaking to the outlet, that the studio is working on an unannounced XCOM game that has had a challenging development, with the team recently missing an important development milestone. This project, if it releases, will be the first Firaxis-developed XCOM game since XCOM: Chimera Squad in 2020.

Firaxis’ most recent release is Civilization VII, which launched in February 2025 to favorable reviews but initially "slow" sales, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick last August.  The game currently has a Mixed reception on Steam after Firaxis spent the last year updating the game to address player complaints. Before Civilization VII, Firaxis shipped Marvel's Midnight Suns in 2022, another critically well-received game that failed to meet sales expectations.

#4096. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4095. Grand Theft Auto VI Review - Outrageous Fortune

Many superlatives will be heard in the discussion around Grand Theft Auto VI – biggest world, most activities, best graphics, deepest narrative – but its real triumph is the way all those features and others work in service of a cohesive, believable immersion in a criminal fantasy that is hard to grasp until you’ve played it for yourself.

Rockstar’s latest returns players to a dramatically expanded version of the Vice City seen in a prior game, now largely unrecognizable after real and in-game years have passed. Leonida is a joy to explore, filled with a wealth of activities, both mundane and illicit. The game’s design makes many ordinary tasks as compelling as the illegal ones. Go fishing off the boat, brew coffee to wake up, work out at the gym, scuba dive for long-lost treasure, dust crops, motocross in the mud, go dancing at the club. As you move between those activities, the world feels alive with minor events, from traffic accidents to shady individuals a little too interested in your walk to the ATM. GTAVI delights in life's minutiae, with animations, voice lines, and background characters that keep things fresh even dozens of hours into the story. The level of detail everywhere is astounding and, at times, overwhelming. Getting sidetracked is easy.

The focus on detail carries into the visuals. Lucia’s hair blows in the wind, and she absently pushes it back behind her ear. A drug den is littered with paraphernalia and empty containers. A shifty contact quirks a smile – your only hint that things are about to go south. Sweat glistens on your character’s skin after a hard workout, their breathing and heart rate noticeably heightened. Clouds roll together in the sky, creating realistic weather simulations. The commitment to an authentic simulated world is encompassing, thoughtful, and intentional, a testament to hand-crafted and meticulously painstaking development work, paying off in an absorbing play-space that is hard to step away from.

While the day-to-day simulation is fascinating, it also adds pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward. Not even one of these meticulously choreographed sequences deserves to be spoiled; they run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect.

Ranged combat is punchy and enjoyable; smart use of cover and time-slowing focus makes most battles manageable. On-foot navigation is in a similar boat – simple to pick up and uninterested in needless complexity or challenge; the focus is on choosing smart moments for stealth, knowing when to run and when to fight, and selecting the precise instant for a burst of sudden action. Driving is fast and intense, made more appealing by a huge variety of functionally distinct vehicles to enjoy. If there’s a fault to the core and optional story missions, it’s that many feel a bit on rails regarding where to go and what to do at each step. At the same time, that directed approach keeps the pace relentless, and the action and outcomes thrilling. Over many hours, the game morphs and throws new wrenches into the mix at key junctures, teasing and then playing out criminal experiences from petty theft to group heists to illicit spec ops, and punctuates those distinct vibes with memorable and singular moments.

Like its predecessors, GTAVI simultaneously lampoons and celebrates life in modern America, taking aim at targets like social media, wellness lifestyles, rap and music culture, manosphere content, and dozens more. The caricatures land so well because, in many cases, they’re (sadly) barely over the line of the absurdity we see reflected in real life, and because Rockstar so ably captures individual subcultures, dialects, and situations. Behind it all is a scathing critique of wealth inequality and the inherent unfairness of a system that sets most up to fail. It’s a bitter message delivered in honey-wrapped, exhilarating gameplay, but it shines through.

Of all its significant feats, the relationship between Lucia and Jason elevates the game to new heights, lending this installment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries. This is, without a doubt, video gaming’s most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you’re left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts. The two collectively suffer the slings and arrows of a world that always seems stacked against them; the fortune they amass is not a power grab, but a desperate attempt to cling to each other and come out the other side together, and the player can’t help but cheer them on and dread how fate might stand in the way.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love.

Alex Van Aken contributed to this article.

Elena Chapella is a Writer for DualShockers. Previously an award-winning journalist, Elena is passionate about writing what she loves.

To say that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the most anticipated game of the year is a colossal understatement, with the game already pulling in billions of dollars in pre-order revenue. However, that doesn’t mean everyone is going to be playing it.

Players could be waiting for a few patches before getting it for themselves (rather than dealing with any potential game-breaking bugs upon release), waiting for the game to go on sale (rather than paying the $80-100 full price), waiting for it to come to PC, or they may just not be interested. Either way, there are all kinds of reasons that will keep someone from playing GTA6 despite it finally coming out.

Want a world of rich lore and exploration while not having too much time on your hands? We've got you covered.

With that in mind, these players should have something to keep them occupied while others are diving into the huge title. They could play other games that recently came out, especially since this year has seen many incredible releases.

So while everyone else continues to carry the hype of GTA6, you can show other 2026 entries the same amount of love.

If you were to break open any open world game to see what lives inside, you’d find a lot of the typical elements: quest-giving NPCs, tons of exploration, a healthy amount of combat and challenge. You get that with Crimson Desert if you were to crack open its world, but you also get some of the most unique expressions an open world can take.

The game is anything but a typical open world game, with zero slog to dredge through and an unparalleled approach to such a massive world. Seriously, as massive as GTA6 is, you’re going to be spending an equal amount of time (if not a little more) in Crimson Desert’s world.

This is one of those games where you need a good amount of time to properly sit with it, wandering the world and taking its challenge like a champ. It’s not like other open world games where you can get an idea of the world based on 15 minutes of gameplay, you’re going to need closer to 15 months before you can cement your opinion.

But I’ll just spoil the opinion for you: it’s going to be so, so cool, to where you’re going to actually be upset about it being snubbed at The Game Awards.

If you grew up playing the Halo games, you’d be pleased to see that Halo: Campaign Evolved is everything you loved about them and then some. Not only is it an incredibly faithful remake for newcomers, but it also adds new content for veteran fans, meaning everybody has something they can properly enjoy.

Its singleplayer focus may be irksome for many FPS fans, but if you adored the original campaign, you’re in for the time of your life.

So sure, you may have waited 13 years for GTA6, but your inner child waited forever to feel that same magic from Halo again – and once you give the remake a chance, you absolutely will feel it throughout your entire soul.

Just don’t think about the current state of Halo, it’s better to live in ignorant bliss.

Silent Hill has been on an incredible winning streak lately, and it’s not looking to be stopping anytime soon, especially with the series’ newest entry. Silent Hill: Townfall is the most recent entry in the franchise, and it’s already carrying the torch (and tone) wonderfully.

Taking place in St. Amelia (a fictional island town in Scotland) rather than the titular town, you play as Simon Ordell as he goes through the tragedy of what happened there. Plus, you have to sneak around and hide to avoid monsters, a slight shift away from the typical survival horror tactics that the series has featured so far.

The entire game is an unforgettable experience from start to finish, with intricate and creative puzzles that will genuinely stump you and music that only amplifies your tense mood. Combine this with the incredible narrative (as standard for the franchise), deep characters (that too) and a new point of view, it’s a game that will stick with you.

If anything, if you’re a hardcore Silent Hill fan like I am, this game will just get you all the more excited for the upcoming Silent Hill Remake and future original titles.

It’s natural to feel protective over children, even in video games – but here comes Pragmata, putting you in charge of the child-robot Diana. You're not ready for the emotional bond.

As you and Diana explore the abandoned lunar base taken over by hostile AI, there are all kinds of things that you both can do: hacking, running and gunning, upgrading your abilities, teaching Diana the ways of humanity, and even dancing.

I just wish we could dance along with Diana; dancing is a joy that’s meant to be shared, and it’s far more fun to jump around with others, especially if we’re dancing with our robot daughter in space.

But as you’re both trying to get out of space and back to Earth together, you’re going to feel warm and fuzzy at every interaction along the way. It's also just an engrossing, action-packed, and creative adventure, from a new IP.

In the past few years, we’ve seen an increase in “dark wuxia” style of games, and Phantom Blade Zero seems to be our newest release in the subgenre. It’s an action game set in a literal phantom world, and you are armed with countless types of blades to help you along your journey … oh, and you’re also killer at kung-fu.

Devs describe the game as “kungfupunk,” and it’s honestly the perfect description of it. It looks good, feels good, plays good – it’s a fun time all around, with the added bonus of impeccable aesthetics from an alternate, dark fantasy version of China’s Ming Dynasty. It creates an action game that sets the bar, a new standard for games to look up to.

It walks a delicate balance between a genuine challenge and action-packed fun, and players would be happy with the entire gameplay experience.

Combined with incredible cinematography, and we have a contender for Game of the Year that’s more than well-deserved. Regardless of what players believe the Game of the Year should be, I firmly believe that this game should win, at the very least, Best Action Game and Best Art Direction.

From bizarre indies to daring blockbusters, these are the ten most extravagant video games of 2026.

Fans of the first Control game have been eagerly waiting for a sequel that’s as good as the original, and that’s exactly what we get with Control Resonant. Instead of playing as Jesse Faden, you actually play as her brother, Dylan, as he tries to save New York from anomalies – but don’t worry if you were a fan, you’ll still see her.

Cool, action-packed and undeniably wild, fans of the first Control will be happy to see that the sequel kept everything they know and love, as well as adding so much more extra flavouring (and breathtaking graphics).

It’s a direct continuation, but amplifies everything to be just better than before, including the clear Stephen King inspiration. In fact, most players are going to find themselves liking this game more than the first.

Just saying, there’s a reason that it’s a contender for Game of the Year and several other categories – and I would honestly say that it’s more than well-deserved. It’s hard to live up to such a unique hype like with Control, yet this game seems to manage the impossible.

While everyone is fighting against the police in GTA6, Gears of War fans have been fighting the Locust Horde for years; in Gears of War: E-Day, we see how this all begins. And if you’ve been a veteran Gears fan, you’re going to be pleased to know that it’s as fun as always – but then again, even if you’re a newer Gears fan, you’re still going to have a great time for entirely different reasons.

By coming to Unreal Engine 5, the game ends up going through much-needed revisions in the gameplay, especially when it comes to verticality. Yet, in spite of the adjustments, it’s still a great return to form.

Some players have complained about bugs and crashes, but they’re actually fairly few and far between, and most have been patched since its release. If one were to dive into the game now, the most they’d run into is Brumak deciding that a building is incredibly fascinating and needs a solid bit of observation.

With that in mind, this is an intense, yet super fun game that players will find a ton of time for, especially if they have been staring at it in their Play Later List.

This year has been a great year for the Resident Evil IP, with a killer movie that continues to be gushed over by fans and this year’s fantastic leading title: Resident Evil Requiem. And, to be completely honest, this is my personal pick for Game of the Year.

The game has you playing as two different characters: Grace Ashcroft, whose sections are the traditional horror experience that will have you genuinely terrified, and Leon Kennedy, whose sections are an action-packed power trip. Together, the two of them have to figure out the truth behind the newest virus, Elpis, and what to do about Raccoon City Syndrome.

It’s action horror in the purest sense: a perfect balance of horror and action, yet maintaining a focus on the horror element first and foremost. It’s executed fantastically, and I don’t think I’ve ever had as much fun playing Resident Evil as I had with Requiem.

If players were to compare all the recent Resident Evil titles in the modern era (including remakes), they’d notice something special about Requiem: it takes the best of all of them, and takes the crown as the best modern entry the series has seen so far. If anything, this makes me incredibly excited for what future RE games have in store.

If you love Star Wars and XCOM, you’re going to be over the moon with Star Wars Zero Company. It’s a genuinely perfect marriage, a blend between the two that will have fans of both IPs weeping with joy.

If you’ve ever wanted to feel like the commander of a clone army, that’s exactly the experience that you’ll have with this game: but you’re not limited to having clones in your party. Your squad can be whoever you want, and you can implement whichever strategies you need to in order to be victorious.

Many players might hear about these kind of real-time strategy games and imagine a top-down, board-like UI rather than anything more dynamic, but that’s not how it is in Zero Company. In fact, the game is incredibly cinematic, immersing you in ways that you normally wouldn’t be if it was any other RTS title.

Basically, if you’re looking for the game to have the ultimate nerd-out with, look no further.

Nintendo knows how to keep a loyal fanbase like with the Zelda franchise, and that grip has only gotten stronger with the recent release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake.

This remake isn’t like the 3DS ports that just improve what’s already there, no, this is a remake that’s rebuilt from the ground-up, and it’s just as incredible as we remember from our childhood. In fact, many fans (including veteran fans of the OG) would argue that it’s better than the original. Of course, there are purists, but purists will always have purist takes.

It’s hard to recapture the magic of the original, yet somehow, the remake manages to make the game feel even more magical, but with more updated gameplay (more reminiscent of Breath of the Wild) for modern players and better graphics. Seriously, what is not to love about a classic like this one?

Personally, I do think that Zelda can (and very likely will) outperform GTA6 at The Game Awards, because while GTA6 was easily the most anticipated game of all time, Ocarina of Time was, is, and always will be the most iconic game of all time.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the most beloved games of all time, but these remakes might be just as meaningful to fans.

#4092. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

#4090. Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Tops "Best-Selling" Games In October (US)

CoD has dominated for 19 consecutive years in its debut month

October was another action-packed month for 2026, with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 dropping on Switch 2, and other titles such as Nintendo Switch Sports Resort & Final Fantasy Resonance also releasing.

The charts for the US market are now in, revealing the "projected top 10 best-selling video games" of the month. The Call of Duty series has also hit its 19th consecutive year as the best-selling game in its debut month. Here's the rundown via Circana's senior director and video game industry adviser Mat Piscatella. No sales figures are provided.

"October 2026 U.S. Video Game Market Highlights Thread from Circana - Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was the best-selling game of October, marking the 19th consecutive year that a Call of Duty franchise release has been the best-selling game of its debut month."

Circana has also shared an update on the "projected top 10 best-selling video games" of 2026 so far in the US. Call of Duty: Black Ops II is in sixth on this chart. Meanwhile, Nintendo's Switch title Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream remains in 8th place. The same game has already sold more than eight million units globally (approx 8.81 million) since launching in April.

Piscatella also notes how Switch 2 hardware led in "unit and dollar sales" during October and 2026 year-to-date. Nintendo's "limited edition" Zelda 40th anniversary Switch 2 Pro Controller also led the month in "accessory dollar sales". Again, no sales figures were provided.

And that's it for October 2026! November will reveal how Zelda: Ocarina of Time and GTA 6 have performed. Earlier this week, prior to the launch of GTA 6, it was revealed the Ocarina remake was crowned the best-selling physical game of 2026 in the US.

If you want to find out more about Call of Duty's return to Nintendo platforms, you can check out our Switch 2 review of Modern Warfare.

#4089. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4087. Donnie's Sunken Boat Location In GTA 6

In Grand Theft Auto 6, there are plenty of tasks that Jason gets sent to do in the early game. He gets sent around by and for Brian, oftentimes cleaning up Donnie's messes. One such mess is a boat that Donnie sank off the coast of Corsair Key that had some illicit substances left in it.

However, the game only gives you a search radius and doesn't show the boat's exact location. While it's not so large that it's impossible to find, it can be tough to spot on the ocean floor. This mission is one that's definitely best left for the daytime.

To find where Donnie sunk his boat, you'll have to make your way off the east coast of Corsair Key. You'll have the search area marked on the map once the quest unlocks, and you can take a boat or jetski out to the area and try to find it. Luckily, there's one of each at Jason's house that you can take.

It's helpful to have scuba gear with you, but it isn't necessary.

Once you're in the circle, make your way to the spot on the map that's shown in the first image above. You'll be able to tell that you're in the right place by all the floating debris that's in the area. There's a lot of it scattered around, but the highest concentration of debris is right above where the boat sank.

Press the right bumper or R1 to dive below the surface and swim all the way down to the ocean floor. When you spot the boat, it'll be on its side, with contents spilled all over. The bricks won't be randomly strewn across the ocean floor, and there's no reason to hang around because there's no other loot in the area.

Here is where to locate the giant crab, get the Crabshack VF5, and unlock the safe in GTA 6.

To find the contents of the boat that you're searching for, you'll have to get right up close to the boat itself. There are three compartments that you can interact with: one behind the driver's seat, and two along what would be the floor of the boat.

When you open the compartment behind the seat, some fish will swim out and there won't be anything you can collect in there. Instead, go to the floor compartment towards the rear of the boat, and that's where you'll find the bricks that you're looking for. If you search the forward compartment, you won't find anything.

After you've got the bricks, simply swim back up to the surface and take them to Brian's lockup to get some money back for them. Luckily, you can do this whole mission without attracting any attention from the police, so it should be smooth sailing the whole way. At least, smoother than that boat ride was for Donnie.

If you want to get around Leonida and clear GTA 6's map with ease, Auto-Drive is one of your best friends.

#4086. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#4085. Toby Fox Shares Deltarune Chapter 6 And 7 Development Update

Toby Fox, the creator of Deltarune (and Undertale), has this week released his 'Fall 2026' newsletter, giving fans a "status update" on Chapter 6...and Chapter 7.

Firstly, Chapter 6 is "progressing well", and the game is now a "structurally complete draft" that can be played from start to finish. In saying this, it will still take a "bit longer" to finish up some other scenes and details:

"Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.

"Even though Chapter 6 is a rather short chapter, I would like it to be as good as possible. I won't be able to rush this."

As for the recent vote, Queen is officially the winner, taking out 65% of the votes. And the reward is a "stupid scene" from Chapter 6.

And if this wasn't already enough, there's the Chapter 7 development update. The team has "only just started", and Fox has read out some of the events and dialogue to the team, but is withholding the rest of the story until they "complete more of the game".

I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens.

Team members who completed their work on Chapter 6 have moved onto Chapter 7 now. Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!

Fox ends the latest update, reminding fans how the team has expanded since Chapter 4, but "more and more time is necessary" to keep the game's development going at the "fastest pace possible". The next update will apparently take place when the localization of Chapter 6 is done.

#4084. Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

After dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game. But for my part, the feature that elevated the game most prominently above Rockstar Games’ other (excellent) games wasn’t its graphics, missions, or action – it was the storytelling and interplay between the two lead protagonists. Jason and Lucia bring heart, emotional depth, and a sense of genuine threat to the crime fantasy, as you grow attached to them and start cheering for them against all the odds stacked against them.

We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.

During my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida. Was a couple or romantic relationship the plan or goal for the game from very early on in development, or did that come later? Do you see the focus on Jason and Lucia’s relationship as one of the features that separates Grand Theft Auto VI from your prior work on storytelling in the game series?

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design: “The dual protagonists and the relationship between the two of them was there from very early in development, but exactly how that was expressed in the game did change over time. It was an enormous challenge for us to get them working together in the open world together and finding exactly how that would work. As we started to layer in more mechanics, dialogue, and incremental features across all teams, it just clicked at some point. The ability to be together in the open world also allowed us for new ways to tell the story of the game and to bring some of the exposition and narrative into the open world in a way we hadn’t been able to do before. Hearing these little bits of dialogue as you are just tooling around the world that have specific context to what you as a player have just been doing in the story really knits it all together.”

The player has a choice for how to develop the relationship between the two leads, but I imagine most players are drawn toward helping it thrive. In early playtests, is that what you observed?

Katie Pica, Design Director: Player Systems & Progression:“Overall, we’ve seen that players are invested in supporting Jason and Lucia’s relationship but we don’t favor a specific path through the game, it is completely down to player choice.”

It feels like a lot of the game’s driving narrative beats factor for a close connection between Jason and Lucia. Was it challenging to craft variations that included a more tense or distant connection between the two? Is that even possible?

Luke Howard, Senior Design Director: Missions & Visualization:“One of the core goals of this game was to tell the story of Jason and Lucia with a base line relationship where they are amicable, if just platonic, as they still share the same ultimate goals and need each other to achieve them. So, this gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist. In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile.

One example is after Lucia helps Kordell’s gang pull off an intense armored truck robbery she shares the information with Raul’s crew. Afterwards Jason pulls Lucia aside to see how she's coping. This moment carries several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them. The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia.”

Were there any fictional couples or real-life couples that the team looked at for inspiration in shaping the Jason and Lucia dynamic, whether those couples came from big crime stories or not?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“We definitely started by looking at all the “couple on the run” movies. There are a lot of them but the ones that we kept coming back to were Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in Bonnie and Clyde, McQueen and MacGraw in The Getaway (the Jim Thomson book is also great), True Romance, Thelma and Louise. Clooney and JLo’s dynamic in Out of Sight, as well. And then a lot of buddy movies actually – Riggs and Murtaugh, Butch and Sundance, Mike Lowry and Marcus Burnett, etc. for their back and forth together. In terms of having a game where the characters can change based on how you play and whether you really lean into and enjoy the crime spree we thought about how both Pulp Fiction and Natural Born Killers start with a couple in a diner pulling out guns, but then how different those couples are and how different those scenarios play out. Jason and Lucia are a lot tougher than Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer but we liked the idea of telling a story where Jason and Lucia could end up being closer to either end of that spectrum based on what the player was doing.”

Sex and intimacy are notoriously complicated and challenging to present in games. How did you aim to strike a balance with their private moments together that felt authentic? Any thoughts about how or why it’s so challenging to present adult relationships in video games?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“This is definitely something we thought a lot about and spent a long time trying to get right. The actors who play Jason and Lucia were so good, and they had a natural chemistry and part of it was just trying to capture some of that.

There’s this trade off in making games between player control and then scripted scenarios. We try and give the player as much control as we can because we are working in an interactive medium and actually doing something rather than watching it is going to feel more powerful. But then you have the ability to really mess around and break the illusion of a tender or romantic moment or whatever it is. So the relationship aspect of this story is there if a player wants to engage in it, but if they don’t the story can play out differently.”

In its best moments of genuine support, regular connection, open communication, and flirty or engagement with one another, Jason and Lucia can come across as a pretty ideal model of good relationships – even while they’re simultaneously committing major crimes together. Was that juxtaposition of a healthy romantic relationship against an external world of illicit activity an explicit goal for how the narrative came together?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“That was the goal, yes. You are really living with these characters – they’re eating, sleeping, showering, throwing away their trash, or not. The relationship needed to feel real to sit alongside all of that. Then even just as a development team, we live with these characters for years and years. We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for. And they needed to like each other. But then the world itself is so crazy and chaotic and seemingly on the brink of collapse.

When we set out to make this game, and go into that multiyear development marathon, we said we wanted to spend our time working on something with heart, and with some characters you could care about and root for. It’s barely worth even stating, but we are living in a time when people are divided along almost every line, and feelings about the future are pretty bleak. We wanted to create a world that held up a mirror to that, showed that fever pitch of craziness that we are all maybe a couple of bad decisions away from, but we wanted the story we were going to tell to have something positive at its core and the message that human connection is better than division.”

The game automatically moves you to play one character or another at certain points, but for many sequences, you can choose your playable lead. In your experience playing and watching others play, do most players gravitate toward one character or another as “their character?”

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design:“It really varied in our playthroughs. They are both such great characters and performances that people seemed to gravitate to both of them in different ways. But overall, we have found the split of time between characters to be relatively even on a per-playthrough and also at a macro level.”

#4083. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

#4082. Why Do I Want To Paint The Walls In Grand Theft Auto VI?

I admire the cozy sim genre. Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing are on regular rotation in my home on my family’s screens, but not my own. In an odd way, I find the genre stressful, arguably the opposite of its intended purpose. I will happily and cathartically guide Grace Ashcroft through the tense hallways of Rhodes Hill in Resident Evil Requiem, but Pokémon Pokopia’s seemingly endless list of to-dos makes me sweat. It’s just not my genre, and I have come to terms with that.

Grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics. Bird (and animal) watching, for example, is apparent and encouraged early in the experience. You can also fix up your somewhat dilapidated home from almost the moment you are let loose outside of the opening tutorial missions.

And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.

I climbed to the roof to fix the leak and replaced all the stairs leading up to the home before I ever participated in the game’s namesake and stole a car. Normally, it’s the kind of interaction I skip or choose not to engage with, given the option. Or, I do the bare minimum to progress. Sure, I have all the options in the world to build and decorate a house and make it my own, but… that feels like a lot of work. And I am not an artist.

The “cozy” elements of Grand Theft Auto VI are admittedly different from those in a game like Pokopia or Animal Crossing. You’re not designing your home (though you can pick a paint color), but it feels similar, and I am trying to figure out why I enjoy it here as opposed to other games. Is it because Jason and Lucia are so instantly believable as human beings that I want their home to be nicer?

After some thought, I think it might just come down to Grand Theft Auto VI’s consistently impressive visual fidelity. Replacing the shingles on the roof, for example, offers a close-up look at Jason’s character model, and you can practically feel the texture of the asphalt while the heat of the sun beats down.

I don’t have confirmation, but it also just feels like someone at Rockstar did exhaustive research on what the process of replacing a roof shingle should look like, even if, I’m sure, it probably doesn’t quite work that way in the real world. Jason makes it look incredibly easy, to the point that it had me questioning if I should be climbing up to my own roof and taking care of some loose shingles myself. And you know what is a lot of fun? Watching someone who is good at something do the thing they’re good at.

I’m now into the driving and shooting part of the game (and enjoying that, too!), but I am shocked at how grateful I was to have the option to stay home and put up drywall.

#4081. Where To Find The Marbelle Hotel Safe Code In GTA 6

Here is how to find the Silent Hill easter egg and Marbelle Hotel safe code in GTA 6.

There are a lot of easter eggs and references throughout Grand Theft Auto 6. While some are more well-hidden than others, a few can be easily stumbled across even if you're not looking for them.

One of these is the Marbelle Hotel in Vice City, which is an unremarkable-looking building that's hiding a pretty spooky experience inside. Here is where to find it, how to trigger the easter egg, where the Marbella Hotel Safe code is, and if you get anything for your troubles.

If you're looking to find this easter egg, you will need to first make your way to Vice City in the center of the map. Once you arrive, head to the Crosstown district and go south towards the Pawn & Gun — Crosstown store. Just east of this store, about a block away, will be the Marbelle Hotel, which is a small three-story building that has a pretty worn and old facade. The front door will be locked, so head around the back and use the unlocked door.

Gotta make the place look nice for the big homecoming.

Once inside, you will see a safe on your right, but we don't have the code right now, so instead head up the stairs. When you reach the third floor, the door will open on its own (I'm sure it's fine), but don't go inside right away.

Instead, loop around the railing by the stairs to find a Ratface card on the old dresser in the corner. When you're ready, head through the door that opened and attempt to go up to the roof via the small staircase. Unsurprisingly, the door behind you will shut and lock, trapping you in this stairwell.

A bunch of spooky symbols and drawings will then appear all over the walls around you, and a heavy fog will flood the hotel and surrounding area. After a few seconds, the doors will unlock, but your visibility will be heavily limited due to the fog. Don't panic; there are actually no enemies or monsters you need to deal with.

Once the doors open, go onto the roof of the hotel and walk forward when you exit. On the ground, there will be a notepad that will give you a lot of lore about the Marbelle Hotel, along with the safe code, which is circled near the bottom of the notepad. You can also see the code briefly when all the symbols appear on the wall!

Now, head back downstairs and go to the safe and enter the code 955214. Doing so will unlock the safe, which contains some cash along with the legendary Cash and Crowex Ambassador Breakfast watch that you can use on either Jason or Lucia.

You will now be free to leave, as there are no more secrets outside of a pipe you can use as a melee weapon, which is another reference to Silent Hill, since it's a classic weapon throughout the franchise. Additionally, this will unlock the "The Truth Is Out There" trophy, which requires you to encounter one of a few specific supernatural occurrences.

Though there are hundreds of voices and talented actors in Grand Theft Auto 6, here are a few that you'll be hearing the most!

#4080. Grand Theft Auto VI's Auto Drive Is A Beautiful And Free Version Of Hands-Free Travel

Grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Always has been. But sometimes, you just won't feel like actively driving, but you also don't to waste money on a cab.

This is where Auto Drive comes in. It lets the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky "having to pay attention to the road." Red Dead Redemption 2 had the same feature, and I have fond memories of taking advantage of it to watch Arthur ride his horse through that game's incredible environment. It's a great option in GTAVI, but how to use it and turn it on isn't immediately apparent.

First, you must select a destination. Get the GPS set up to direct you to where you want to go.

Next, start driving. The Auto Drive is smart, but doesn't seem to be smart enough to make three-point turns or back out of parking lots. You need to be on your way before you can turn it on.

Once you're on the path, hold down in the d-pad and press start to activate Cinematic.

Once you've done this you should be able to hold down the Circle button on PlayStation or the B button on Xbox to activate Auto Drive and... voilà! You can sit back and let Jason or Lucia take the wheel. They will drive legally, even stopping at lights, but you can speed them up if they're taking too long.

I've always enjoyed driving in Grand Theft Auto, but I was grateful to find this almost-hidden option early in the game.

#4079. Tripwire Interactive says it's laying off 36 staff in a "necessary" decision, while reassuring that Killing Floor 3 and Maneater 2 are still in active development

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find new jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.
